newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Vasectomy for a snip at New Zealand charity auction.
newsitem.headline: Vasectomy for a snip at New Zealand charity auction.

text.p: A New Zealand mother of six was the successful bidder for a vasectomy at a charity auction held in the South Island coastal town of Blenheim, the New Zealand Press Association reported on Monday.
The operation, donated by a local surgeon, was one of dozens of items on offer at a fundraiser for a magnetic resonance imager (MRI) scanner for the local hospital.
The vasectomy fetched NZ$330 (US$230) from the lucky mother, who wished to remain anonymous.
She said she did not make the bid in person because she was unable to get a baby-sitter for her large brood.
The women present at the auction got into the spirit of things and there was enthusiastic bidding for the "private cut" vasectomy, said auction organiser Toni Gillan.
A few concerned men protested light-heartedly by leaving the room. But they were lured back by the more romantic items on offer such as magnums of champagne, deer velvet liqueur and dinners for two.
The election night event raised more than NZ$9,000 for the scanner.
